title: bug: set_task_status BLOCKED → blockedFromStatus re-assigns the row to its recorded assignee unconditionally, unlike the dependency and resource auto-unblocks, which keep it only for a worker that exists, is not DEAD and still points at the task. A manual unblock after the blocked-timeout idled a resource-parked seat therefore strands the row on that corpse: unclaimable, unalerted, never pruned
description:
Filed by hunt #14 (task-d5d58972, 2026-11-03, architect-1dd28c7c). Lane: dead-worker handling. This is one path skipping a rule its two siblings apply.

PROBLEM (HEAD 942717bc)
- The contract is in packages/moe-daemon/CLAUDE.md:7: the dependency auto-unblock "restores a still-assigned hold to its worker only while that worker exists, is not DEAD and still points at the task — else the task returns unassigned".
- Both automatic restores implement it:
  - packages/moe-daemon/src/state/dependencyUnblock.ts:255-267. Its comment names this exact starvation: an IDLE record with no pointer is neither missing nor DEAD, so isTaskClaimable stays false, while the Layer-3 prune refuses a worker that "owns active work". That lasts until a daemon restart, with no alert.
  - state/resourceStore.ts:570-573 (resumeResourceHolder): "Mirror dependency-unblock: a timed-out or repurposed worker no longer owns this hold."
- The manual restore skips it. tools/setTaskStatus.ts:209-215: when the target equals effectiveFrom (the blockedFromStatus), it does `updates.assignedWorkerId = task.assignedWorkerId` with no owner check.
- The daemon creates the stranded state itself:
  - The blocked-timeout sweep keeps a resource-waiting BLOCKED row assigned (state/sweeps.ts:456-460; its bound is the lease reaper).
  - It then sets the timed-out seat IDLE with currentTaskId null (sweeps.ts:485-489).
  - unblock_worker cannot reach that row afterwards, because it requires worker.status BLOCKED (tools/unblockWorker.ts:48-50). So set_task_status (or the board's drag, which uses the same tool semantics) is the manual route, and docs/roles/governor.reference.md:31 offers it ("task-only, moe.set_task_status").
- Result: the row goes back to WORKING assigned to the IDLE corpse. No agent can claim it, no sweep alerts on it, the corpse is never pruned, and its running attempt stays open. A restart then holds it a further reconcileWindowMs, and only a manual release_task recovers it.

EVIDENCE
- Repro: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-d5d58972/A/zzHuntA_manualUnblockCorpse.test.ts, run from packages/moe-daemon/src/__hunt__/ of a `git archive 942717bc` snapshot.
- Setup: a resource-parked seat silent 2 h. The real `state.checkBlockedTimeouts()` runs (the row stays BLOCKED and assigned, and the seat goes IDLE with currentTaskId null). Then `set_task_status {taskId, status:'WORKING'}` runs with no workerId, i.e. the human path.
- `npx vitest run src/__hunt__/zzHuntA_manualUnblockCorpse.test.ts` → 1 failed:
  AssertionError: expected 'worker-parked' to be null      (task.assignedWorkerId)
  AssertionError: expected false to be true                (state.isTaskClaimable(task))
  AssertionError: expected true to be false                (state.hasActiveTaskAssignment(corpse), so Layer 3 never prunes it)
- The architect re-ran it at 23:28Z with the same three failures. The output is in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-d5d58972/A/manualUnblockCorpse.vitest.txt.
- Exposure: rare. It needs a dead resource-parked seat silent past blockedTimeoutMs (1 h), then a manual unblock. But the strand is silent and only release_task undoes it. If the seat's wrapper is in fact alive, its next claim resumes the row (alreadyAssigned), which is why the keep-arm must stay for a live, pointing seat.

FIX DIRECTION
- On the return-to-blockedFromStatus arm, keep the assignee only when `state.getWorker(id)` exists, its status is not DEAD, and its currentTaskId === task.id. Otherwise write assignedWorkerId null.
- updateTask's hand-back then closes the running attempt, as MCP_SERVER.md "Close on hand-back" describes.
- Put the predicate in ONE exported helper in state/dependencyUnblock.ts (for example `parkedHoldOwner(state, task): string | null`) and use it from dependencyUnblock.ts and setTaskStatus.ts. resourceStore.ts may adopt it too, but that is optional; keep the diff small.
- Do not change the BLOCKED-entry arm (setTaskStatus.ts:~196, which keeps the seat when blocking) or any other exit arm.
- Docs (this row's own section, ruling msg-71db57ac): update the `### moe.set_task_status` "Attempts:" sentence in docs/MCP_SERVER.md (about :1671). It currently says "returning from BLOCKED to blockedFromStatus keep the seat and so keep its attempt". It should say the seat is kept only while that worker exists, is not DEAD and still points at the task; otherwise the row returns unassigned and its attempt closes. Edit only that section.

FILES (planner to confirm)
- packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/setTaskStatus.ts
- packages/moe-daemon/src/state/dependencyUnblock.ts (export the shared predicate)
- packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/setTaskStatus.unblockOwner.test.ts (new)
- docs/MCP_SERVER.md (### moe.set_task_status only)

OUT OF SCOPE: sweeps.ts (its own row, the blocked-timeout lastActivityAt stamp, is filed alongside this one, with no shared file); packages/moe-daemon/CLAUDE.md (held by task-5158e85b, and it already states the rule); unblock_worker; the /ws handlers.

VERIFICATION (in a git-archive snapshot, never in place): `cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/tools/setTaskStatus src/state/dependencyUnblock.test.ts`
definitionOfDone: New test setTaskStatus.unblockOwner.test.ts runs the real checkBlockedTimeouts on a resource-parked seat silent past blockedTimeoutMs, then calls set_task_status (no workerId) back to blockedFromStatus. It asserts assignedWorkerId null, state.isTaskClaimable(task) true, the task's running attempt closed, and hasActiveTaskAssignment(corpse) false.

The same test keeps the genuine hold: a non-DEAD assignee whose currentTaskId names the row keeps the assignment on the return to blockedFromStatus. A DEAD, missing, or no-longer-pointing assignee yields null. dependencyUnblock.ts and setTaskStatus.ts call one shared predicate rather than two copies.

docs/MCP_SERVER.md's `### moe.set_task_status` Attempts sentence states the alive-and-pointing rule, and no other section changes. In a snapshot, `cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/tools/setTaskStatus src/state/dependencyUnblock.test.ts` exits 0.
